items.work: Il barbiere di Siviglia — complete opera
items.performers: Teresa Berganza, Hermann Prey, Luigi Alva, Enzo Dara, Paolo Montarsolo; Ambrosian Opera Chorus; London Symphony Orchestra; Claudio Abbado
items.label: Deutsche Grammophon
items.note: Ruffo’s Figaro and the overture in the Hall come from a much larger comedy. The complete opera also has the duets in which the plot is laid and the first-act finale, where the characters’ separate anxieties combine in a single rhythmic ensemble. It is the first complete Barber to own, with Berganza singing Rosina with poise and agility and Abbado keeping the action moving and giving the ensembles room to articulate every syllable.

items.work: Guglielmo Tell — complete opera, Italian version
items.performers: Sherrill Milnes, Luciano Pavarotti, Mirella Freni, Nicolai Ghiaurov; Ambrosian Opera Chorus; National Philharmonic Orchestra; Riccardo Chailly
items.label: Decca
items.note: The overture does not include Tell’s ordeal as a father or Arnold’s divided loyalties, which belong to the full opera. This recording, with Milnes, Pavarotti and Freni, uses the Italian translation in place of Rossini’s original French text. Its cast is strong, with Pavarotti as Arnold, and the recording leads beyond the overture into the opera’s long-phrased vocal writing.
